slot.brief: Rank three species (e.g., SF4, XeF4, ClF3-type set) by number of lone pairs on central atom and match to geometry; test VSEPR counting.

stem: For $\text{SF}_4$, $\text{ClF}_3$ and $\text{XeF}_4$, which option gives, in this order, the number of lone pairs on the central atom and the molecular geometry?

verdicts.working: VSEPR: SF₄ is AX₄E (1 lone pair, seesaw); ClF₃ is AX₃E₂ (2 lone pairs, T-shaped); XeF₄ is AX₄E₂ (2 lone pairs, square planar).

working:
Central-atom lone pairs: $\text{SF}_4$: $1$; $\text{ClF}_3$: $2$; $\text{XeF}_4$: $2$. Their molecular geometries are seesaw (5 domains), T-shaped (5 domains), and square planar (6 domains), respectively.

Independent check: VSEPR: SF₄ is AX₄E (1 lone pair, seesaw); ClF₃ is AX₃E₂ (2 lone pairs, T-shaped); XeF₄ is AX₄E₂ (2 lone pairs, square planar).
solution: By VSEPR, $\text{SF}_4$ is $\text{AX}_4\text{E}$ (1 lone pair, seesaw), $\text{ClF}_3$ is $\text{AX}_3\text{E}_2$ (2 lone pairs, T-shaped), and $\text{XeF}_4$ is $\text{AX}_4\text{E}_2$ (2 lone pairs, square planar).
